visual_action: In a comedy sketch set in a dressing room, actress Maya Rudolph, portraying Kamala Harris, looks into a mirror. The real Kamala Harris then appears in the mirror's reflection, surprising Rudolph's character and the live audience. The two women talk and laugh together. At the end of the sketch, they stand side-by-side, arm-in-arm, and smile at the camera before the scene cuts to an aerial shot of a city at night.

cast.name: Kamala Harris
cast.evidence: Kamala Harris appears on screen and is named in the on-screen text, "Kamala makes a surprise appearance on SNL".

on_screen_text.text: Kamala makes a surprise appearance on SNL 😂

spoken_summary: In a Saturday Night Live sketch, actress Maya Rudolph, playing Kamala Harris, wishes she could talk to someone in her shoes. The real Kamala Harris then appears in the mirror. After a lengthy applause, Harris offers encouragement, saying, "You got this." They have a comedic conversation, making jokes about Harris's laugh and using wordplay with her name, such as "end the dramala" and "watch a rom-comala." Harris adds a reference to "Legally Blondela." They conclude by parodying the phrase "Keep Calm and Carry On" as "Keep Kamala and Carry On-ala," and then delivering the show's iconic catchphrase, "And live from New York, it's Saturday Night!"
audio_music: The audio consists entirely of dialogue from the sketch and the prominent reactions of a live studio audience, including loud, sustained applause and frequent laughter.
editing_pacing: The video is a continuous clip from a live television sketch, edited with standard cuts between different camera angles focused on the performers. The pacing is that of a typical comedy sketch.
cultural_references: "Live from New York, it's Saturday Night!" (iconic TV catchphrase)
central_claim: Kamala Harris made a surprise guest appearance on Saturday Night Live, joining her impersonator Maya Rudolph in a comedy sketch.
intended_effect: To portray Kamala Harris as relatable, possessing a good sense of humor, and being culturally engaged by participating in a popular comedy show.
